  • Partial or countrywide ban on large gatherings
  • Mandatory closure of businesses that do not provide or produce essential goods
  • A state of emergency may be in effect in some parts of the country, but this is manifested in emergency funding rather than martial law
  • Restrictions on entry, such as mandatory 14-day self-isolation for anyone entering
  • Restrictions on exports of strategic importance
  • Schools are closed
  • Public transport is closed or severely curtailed
  • Violating restrictions on movement may result in financial penalties or arrest
properties.Civil_Unrest_risk_description:
Indicators:

  • Demonstrations are frequent and may often become large, violent and widespread bouts of unrest.

  • Protests typically devolve into violent confrontations between protesters and police.

  • Demonstrations on some issues are often accompanied by localised violence. 

  • Rioting is sporadic

  • Tensions between different ethnic, religious, social or political groups or communities may be high and sometimes lead to clashes

  • Public trust in government institutions is low, particularly among certain demographic and political interest groups

  • Youth unemployment is probably high and socio-economic conditions are generally poor and are often a source of  unrest or violent dissent

  • The police often respond to demonstrations heavy-handedly

  • The political culture probably avenues for dissent to be expressed freely and the government is generally unwilling to tolerate lawful dissent

  • Laws are not applied and enforced fairly

  • Political participation levels are low and civil society is suppressed

  • Trade union activity may be common, disruptive and militant 

  • A state of emergency may be declared

Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply.
properties.Medical_Public_Health_risk_description:
Indicators:

  • Healthcare services are of a generally high standard in major cities.

  • Access to emergency healthcare services may be difficult in some locations.

  • There may be an ongoing public health emergency of limited impact. For example, an epidemic in a particular area that is being contained at present

  • The capabilities of the state to detect, prevent and respond to public health crises is average by international standards

  • Public sanitation standards are average by international standards.

  • Moderate public health expenditure per capita

  • High quality of care at private hospitals and clinics

  • Quality of care at public hospitals and clinics can be poor outside major cities

  • Specialist surgical treatment is concentrated in only one or two cities

  • Health professionals are generally able to communicate in widely spoken languages

  • Some medicines and specialised medical equipment may be unavailable in parts of the country

  • The WHO has declared a Grade 1 Emergency, meaning that it has minimal public health consequences or that minimal external support is required

  • The CDC has declared a Level 1 Travel Health Notice, meaning that it advises travellers to follow the usual precautions for that destination

  • There may be a localised outbreak of a communicable or other serious infectious disease

  • Health professionals may recommend specialised vaccines prior to travel

  • The proportion of children that receive vaccinations is high but varies countrywide

Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply.
properties.Tectonic_Risks_risk_description:
Indicators

  • Moderate probability of earthquakes occurring per annum (20 - 30%). Expected damage around USD200mn per annum

  • Low possibility of Tsunamis occurring per annum (<5%). Expected damage around USD 5-10mn per annum

  • Moderate probability of volcanic eruptions (5-10% per annum). Moderate damage costs of USD5mn per annum

  • Moderate level of landslide susceptibility based on historical data

Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply.
properties.Governance_Risk_risk_description:
Indicators
  • The government, political system and state institutions are not stable, and can often be ineffective and lacking resilience and public legitimacy
  • The government is inconsistent at formulating, legislating and enacting policy. Public engagement in these processes is very limited and vested interests often influence policy to the detriment of wider public interest
  • Policy implementation is inconsistent and regulation is often weak or inconsistently applied
  • Democratic institutions are immature and vulnerable or exposed to illiberal reforms and change; the system of governance is in a state of transition
  • There is a populist and authoritarian government that has an illiberal agenda and is weakening democratic governance and rights
  • Elections are not free and fair. Elections can often result in violent or destabilising contestations. New government formation may be excessively protracted following elections
  • Rule of law is weak. The judiciary is not independent and is subject to political interference. The law is not always clear, or publicised, or stable or accessible to all
  • There are high levels of state corruption and patronage may be common. There is little transparency and accountability in elected and unelected branches of state
  • State agencies often act arbitrarily and with impunity
  • The government does not have a monopoly on organised armed violence
  • Essential public services, such as police, the judiciary or the civil service are of generally poor quality and low reliability, and may have at times ceased to operate
  • The civil service is not impartial and often ineffectively implements policy
  • Outbreaks of civil unrest and other forms of serious political violence occur often; protest activity is often suppressed
  • The central bank is not fully independent
  • The press is not free and the government exerts a high degree of influence over the media and uses state broadcasters
  • Civil society (including community groups, religious organisations, unions and NGOs) face significant constraints and monitoring, particularly in the areas of press freedom and human or civil rights
Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply. See the Governance Risk map page for more detailed methodology information here.
properties.Cyber_Threat_Exposure_risk_description:
Indicators
  • The volume of cyber attacks reported in the country are higher than the global average
  • The country has high levels of internet, smartphone, social media and e-commerce penetration
  • Underlying structural risk factors point to very high degree of targeting opportunity and attractiveness such as high levels of internet penetration and relative wealth in the population
  • The national cyber security agency frequently advises of the threat of ransomware or malware attacks on organisations, citing past evidence of hostile cyber activity on domestic networks
  • There is precedent of disruptive cyber attacks on one or more strategic/critical infrastructure sectors, and the authorities have struggled to mitigate disruption or recover systems quickly
  • High levels of the active population possess sufficient digital skills, such as computer skills, basic coding or digital reading
  • Hostile state cyber actor(s) are currently intent and capable of disrupting or sabotaging domestic critical infrastructure, organisations and government agencies
  • Hacktivist groups have threatened to target organisations, including data leaks
  • There are indications that hostile state cyber actors are engaged in active disinformation campaigns, which may include attempts to influence elections
  • The authorities have warned about potential exposure of organisations to uncontrolled spread of worm-like malware
Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply. See the Cyber Threat Exposure map page for more detailed methodology information here.
properties.Terrorism_Risk_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • The threat level is to low to moderate. Our analysis and information suggests that terrorists have little to some capability and/or intent to mount an attack or action
  • In the unlikely event of an attack, the capabilities of terrorists are such that attacks are likely to be small scale and of limited or no more than moderate impact
  • Moderate impact means injuries, or single casualties, limited property damage, and localised resultant disruption
  • High impact attacks mean lethal or mass casualty attacks, significant property damage, and resultant widespread disruption and loss of confidence in security beyond the location of the attack
View the Terrorism Threat and Risk maps, and explanatory notes here.
properties.Corruption_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Reported cases of petty or high level corruption are fairly common
  • The rule of law is weak
  • Public service provision is of a poor quality
  • Regulations are often excessive
  • Officials are rarely held accountable for misconduct
  • Anecdotal evidence indicates state representatives expect abnormal cash ‘facilitation payments’ or other personal rewards
  • Administrative procedures are non-transparent and difficult to navigate
  • Processing times for official activity, such as for operating licences and permits, are unclear and often not adhered to and can lead to solicitations for bribes
  • There is a lack of political will to address malfeasance in the public sector
  • There is a reasonably large informal economy
View the Corruption risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Interstate_Conflict_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Peaceful international relations
  • No territorial or sovereignty disputes or adversarial relations with other states
  • Neighbouring or regional powers have no military buildups or offensive capabilities in border areas
  • Large-scale military exercises are infrequent and conducted internationally in a peacetime defence framework as joint exercises with neighbours and allies
  • The government has international legitimacy and recognition
  • The country is party to internationally recognised and functional regional co-operation agreements and/or defence alliances
  • Militarisation of neighbouring countries and in the wider region is low
  • Low levels of defence spending 
  • Military capabilities are entirely defensive
  • Excluding peacekeeping operations, little to no expeditionary military capability or overseas military bases
View the Interstate Conflict risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Civil_Conflict_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • There is likely a history of armed group activity in the country
  • Secessionist, separatist, or other armed political movements may be forming
  • Ethnic or religious grievances may be prompting isolated cases of inter-communal violence
  • Regime instability, terrorism, and civil unrest risk levels are moderate or higher
  • The legitimacy or authority of the government is contested by certain groups
  • The military is not fully professional, stable, cohesive, and disciplined
  • Political instability and civil unrest risk ratings are moderate
  • There is a low risk of conflict spillover or contagion from neighbouring countries
View the Civil Conflict risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Terrorism_Threat_risk_description: Our analysis and information suggests that terrorists have some capability to mount an attack in the area or on the target types indicated, and that such an act would be consistent with their general intent. View the Terrorism Threat and Risk maps, and explanatory notes here.
properties.State_Agencies_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • State agencies have some known intent to target legitimate international companies and organisations in potentially sensitive industries for economic espionage or intelligence gathering
  • The government is known to be suspicious of visitors, expatriates or businesses from particular countries or working in sensitive industries
  • Border agents have in some cases compelled travellers to grant them access to their social media accounts 
  • The host state is not known to have delayed or otherwise interfered with consular access to a detained foreigner or with their legal representation in recent years
  • Any arrests of foreigners on suspicion of espionage or subversion do not appear to involve fabricated and politically-motivated charges
  • Foreign governments provide generic advice on electronic device security or conduct that may attract the attention of the security services
  • The law generally protects the privacy of online activity and communications
  • The law requires private companies to assist state agencies seeking to access the content of encrypted communications, though there is little public evidence of companies being compelled to do so 
  • Human and other basic rights and freedoms are generally respected and protected, but some social, political or interest groups experience suppression
  • The rule of law is reasonably strong. The judiciary is generally impartial and efficient and free of improper influence
  • The corruption risk rating is low to moderate
View the State Agencies risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Infrastructure_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • The quality of infrastructure varies nationally
  • International and domestic airports generally have modern facilities and amenities
  • Key roads and railways are well-maintained, but other areas are neglected and may not meet demand
  • Port infrastructure is generally well-developed, of high capacity and resilient
  • The electricity supply is broadly reliable and resilientTelecommunications networks are fairly extensive and generally well-maintained
  • Fast mobile data connections may be lacking in some parts of the country, particularly remote or rural areas
  • Generally diverse and reliable supply of essential commodities, including food, medicine or fuel
  • The agencies that manage public infrastructure are generally competent and efficient, but corruption may be an issue
View the Infrastructure explanatory notes and risk map here.
properties.Road_Safety_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • A high number of road accident fatalities
  • High traffic volume on unpaved roads, including gravel or dirt surfaces
  • Roads with high traffic volume lack median barriers and guardrails
  • Key roads are sometimes impassable due to heavy rain or dust storms
  • Key roads feature difficult terrain, including winding roads and sharp corners
  • Inadequate number of road signs and traffic lights, even in urban areas
  • Poor nighttime visibility due to inadequate street lighting, even in urban areas
  • Aggressive or careless driving is common and rarely punished
  • The process for obtaining a driving licence is not rigorous nor transparent
  • Small makeshift vehicles or livestock are frequently seen on key roads
  • Public emergency response capabilities are underdeveloped
  • Law enforcement officers often discriminate against foreign drivers
View the Road Safety risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.General_Crime_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Official crime data where available indicates a high incidence or rates of crime
  • Foreign travel advisories indicate a generally moderate to high risk of crime
  • Crime is cited anecdotally as a significant or pressing concern by residents or visitors
  • Petty street crimes and misdemeanors are common
  • Murder and other serious crime rates are a problem in many areas
  • Movement at night is generally unsafe in most areas
View the General Crime risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Organised_Crime_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • There are identified organised criminal groups or networks and their activity may significantly affect business such as counterfeiting, extortion, asset theft and increasing general security risk in some areas
  • Organised criminal activity is common and law enforcement agencies may struggle to counter the problem
  • Organised criminal gangs and organisations may operate openly in some areas with impunity
  • Organised criminal activity tends to be wide ranging, including low-level and some high-level crime, including fraud and financial crime, drug trafficking, street gang activity, extortion, prostitution and people trafficking, and weapons trafficking
  • Criminal gangs engage in open and violent control of territory in some areas
  • Clear evidence of a proliferation of illegal firearms
  • The country is a hub for organised narcotics trafficking
  • Evidence of widespread proliferation and trafficking of illegal firearms
  • High murder rates
  • There is a relatively large informal economy and black market for contraband
  • Corruption Risk levels are moderate to high
  • Rule of law is weak
  • State Agencies risk is moderate to high
View the Organised Crime risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.LGBTQ_Discrimination_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Prevailing social attitudes are generally permissive and liberal
  • Consensual same-sex sexual activity is legal
  • Dissemination of pro-LGBTQ+ material is legal
  • There are laws criminalising discrimination and harassment against LGBTQ+ persons but they are not enforced consistently
  • Some interest, social or political groups experience suppression
  • LGBTQ+ persons in the country face some social stigma, particularly in more conservative areas or regions
View the LGBTQ+ Discrimination risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Kidnap_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Official crime data where available indicates that kidnaps are uncommon but do occur
  • Foreign travel advisories indicate a risk of some types of kidnap, usually limited to certain areas
  • Kidnap is only occasionally cited as a concern by residents or visitors in some areas
  • Most incidents that occur are isolated cases and are non-professional, such a family, acquaintance or child abductions
  • Financially-motivated kidnappings are in nearly all cases opportunistic and of limited duration such as express kidnap
  • General crime, organised crime, state agencies and corruption levels are moderate
View the Kidnap risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Security_Safety_Risk_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Most other risk ratings are negligible to moderate, but some may be higher such as terrorism or general crime
  • Foreign governments have no travel restrictions but advise caution in some or all areas for citizens
  • Foreign governments have diplomatic representation, full staffing usually with dependents, and have no travel restrictions in place for their expatriate staff
  • International organisations/businesses have few, if any, travel restrictions but may require their travellers to follow country-specific safety advice or stay in accommodation that conforms to increased levels of security and safety requirements
  • International organisations/businesses will not usually require expatriate staff to live in approved accommodation or locations or travel locally with security, but may issue security guidance
View the Security and Safety Risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Personal_Cyber_Risk_risk_description:
Indicators
  • Host state agencies have been noted to target citizens or travellers to access their personal sensitive data through physical or digital means, particularly those working in sensitive sectors
  • There is a relatively high degree of targeting opportunity and attractiveness for cyber criminal groups and moderate to high levels of internet usage or wealth in the population.
  • The country has high levels of internet, smartphone, social media and e-commerce penetration
  • The host state is moderate levels of social media surveillance, and is known to sometimes pressure social media platforms to provide user information or take down content
  • The host state is known to possess state-developed or commercial spyware technology, and it is intent on using such technologies on specific groups, such as dissenters or human rights activists
  • There are generally low to moderate levels of government filtering of the internet
  • The host state is known to conduct arrests of online users outside or criminal or extremist-related investigations, though the level of such activity is relatively uncommon
  • The host state has some restrictions on the encryption of personal devices
  • The government does not support personal use exemption of encrypted devices, or it may support this but not necessarily enforce exemption in reality
  • The state agencies risk rating is moderate
  • The organised crime risk rating is moderate
Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply. See the Personal Cyber Risks map page for more detailed methodology information here.
properties.National_Cyber_Resilience_risk_descripti:
Indicators

  • The government provides limited support to a limited range of critical sectors

  • The country ranks fairly low in its preparedness to prevent cyber threats and respond to cyber incidents, based on official and intergovernmental datasets

  • The country has demonstrated little capability to detect, withstand and respond to major cyberattacks on state institutions or critical infrastructure

  • The country does not have a cyber intelligence agency, and the country’s capabilities to detect cyber security threats are limited

  • The country does not have a national cyber resilience strategy although it is moving towards developing one

  • The country lacks regulations on cyber breach disclosures across the board, and enforcement is weak

  • The country has a national CERT, but its capabilities or remit to assisting business sectors on cyber security incidents and vulnerabilities are limited

Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply.

properties.Climatic_Risks_risk_description:
Indicators

  • There are no current warnings or alerts for higher impact climatic events

  • High to severe impact climatic events are historically rare

  • Data indicates relatively low levels of material damage or numbers of people affected due to climatic events in recent years

  • Severe damage and danger caused by cyclonic storms is unlikely in the coming month

  • High-impact floods are unlikely in the coming month

  • Outdoor air pollution is very or extremely unlikely to reach dangerous levels

  • Wildfires are unlikely

  • Extreme temperatures are unlikely

  • Droughts are unlikely to dangerously affect the local population and assets in the coming month

Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply.
properties.Regime_Instability_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Rule of law is strong and checks and balances between the executive, legislature and judiciary are effective and institutionally robust
  • Democratic institutions are mature and stable
  • Power transfers are peaceful, democratic, and constitutional
  • The press is free and civil society is pervasive and active 
  • If the regime is illiberal or authoritarian, it enjoys widespread and entrenched popular support and legitimacy from all civil and military institutions, is long-standing (at least a decade), and will most likely be a traditional form of government such as a monarchy
  • If the regime is illiberal or authoritarian, there are clear and robust constitutional measures for succession and a history of peaceful power transfers 
  • The government has full control over the country and the organs of state
  • Political crises are infrequent
  • The government can pass legislation, and enact policies effectively and according to due process
  • There is a low likelihood of government shutdown, administrative or legislative paralysis, electoral crises, or a cessation of public services, such as by police, the judiciary, or the civil service
View the Regime Instability map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Crisis_Risk_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Our information indicates that a crisis is a very unlikely prospect; we have no credible information that suggests otherwise
  • There is no evidence of a credible threat that may lead to a high impact crisis
  • Relevant local or international official agencies indicate that the risk of major crises events is low
  • Most threat and risk ratings are negligible to moderate; any that are moderate or higher, such as terrorism threat or crime, are unlikely to create acute crisis conditions
  • The government is stable and governance risks are low
  • The state is generally resilient and capable of managing reasonably foreseeable crisis events
  • There is a high degree of political and social resilience and structural stability
  • Geophysical risks are low and major geophysical risk events are uncommon or typically localised
Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply.
properties.Covid19_Restriction_Impacts_risk_descrip:
Indicators:
  • A nationwide directive for people to stay at home or limit non-essential movement
  • Partial or countrywide ban on large gatherings
  • Mandatory closure of businesses that do not provide or produce essential goods
  • A state of emergency may be in effect in some parts of the country, but this is manifested in emergency funding rather than martial law

  • Schools are closed

properties.Civil_Unrest_risk_description:
Indicators:

  • Demonstrations usually occur in a manner consistent with lawful democratic protest

  • Most protests often are of small to moderate scale, infrequent, non-violent and not widespread

  • Large but peaceful demonstrations occur sporadically

  • Demonstrations on some issues may be accompanied by localised violence

  • Rioting is uncommon

  • Public trust in government and democratic institutions is reasonably high but political movements exist with low levels of trust that incite protest

  • Socio-economic conditions are generally good but may be occasionally source of  unrest or violent dissent

  • The police are generally well-trained and disciplined, and able to contain civil disturbances but might respond to demonstrations heavy-handedly

  • Public trust in government institutions is low among certain demographic groups. 

  • The political culture probably lacks avenues for dissent to be expressed freely and the government may be unwilling to tolerate some lawful dissent 

  • There is a perception that laws are not applied and enforced fairly

  • Political participation levels are not very high and civil society may be undeveloped 

  • Trade union activity may be common and occasionally disruptive, but is generally non-militant

Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply.
properties.Medical_Public_Health_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Some healthcare services are of a poor standard. Access to emergency healthcare services may be difficult and unreliable
  • There is at least one public health emergency that requires medical mitigation and other precautions.
  • The capabilities of the state to detect, prevent and respond to public health crises effectively is average to low by international standards
  • Public sanitation standards are average to low by international standards.
  • Low public health expenditure per capita
  • Adequate quality of care at private hospitals and clinics in major cities
  • Many health professionals unable to communicate in widely spoken languages
  • Essential medicines and lifesaving resources are concentrated in major cities
  • Specialist surgical treatment is concentrated in only one city and may not be available in the country for some conditions
  • There may be a localised outbreak of a communicable or other serious infectious disease

  • Global health organisations say the country does not fully adhere to childhood immunisation standards
Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply. View the Medical & Health risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Tectonic_Risks_risk_description:
Indicators
  • One of the least seismically active areas in the world
  • Earthquakes very rarely recorded above magnitude 2.5
  • Seismic hazard data indicates average geographic distribution of Peak Ground Acceleration of around 0.00-0.03 PGA (g)
  • No active or dormant volcanoes
  • Tectonic events tend to be of negligible impact (e.g. very slight tremors)
  • No exposure to tsunami risk, for example a landlocked country
  • Negligible to low Infrastructure Risk
Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply. See the Tectonic Risks map page for more detailed methodology information here.
properties.Governance_Risk_risk_description:
Indicators
  • The government, political system and state institutions are broadly stable, but may sometimes be ineffective and lack resilience and may lack high levels of public legitimacy
  • The government is reasonably effective at formulating, legislating and enacting policy, although public engagement in these processes may be limited and/or vested interests may influence policy to the detriment of wider public interest
  • Policy implementation is generally consistent although regulation may be weak or inconsistently applied
  • Legislative processes may be poor and the legislature may lack independent authority or be hamstrung, making effective legislation difficult to pass
  • Democratic institutions may not be mature or fully consolidated and in a state of transition, and vulnerable to challenges and change or erosion from populist and authoritarian governing parties, or parties that are reasonably likely to win office
  • Elections are not always wholly free and fair, and contestations of election results may be common resulting in brief periods of uncertainty and weakened public confidence in the electoral system
  • Rule of law is the general norm but is not entrenched and may be weak in some areas of governance, or it may be coming under credible attack by populist or authoritarian parties
  • The judiciary is nominally independent but can be subject to political interference. The law is generally clear and publicised, but may not be wholly stable and for some groups may not be applied evenly
  • There are low to moderate levels of state corruption, and there may be weak laws on lobbying that give interest groups a disproportionate influence on policy. Full transparency and accountability is not universal in either the elected or unelected branches of state
  • The government exercises legitimate control over the country and the organs of state, including security agencies such as the military, police and intelligence, although it may not have a full monopoly on the use of organised armed force
  • The civil service is not wholly impartial but effectively implements policy
  • Public services are of reasonable quality and reliability. There may have been rare stoppages in the provision of public services, such as by police, the judiciary or the civil service in recent history
  • Outbreaks of civil unrest and other forms of serious political violence may occur periodically, protests are generally tolerated, although some may be suppressed
  • The central bank may not be fully independent
  • The press is mostly free but the government may exert a degree of influence over some media and may use state broadcasters
  • Civil society (including community groups, religious organisations, unions and NGOs) is active but may face some constraints or monitoring on some issues, particularly press freedom and human or democratic rights
Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply. See the Governance Risk map page for more detailed methodology information here.

  • Smartphone penetration is generally between 10- 50% of the population

  • The country does not appear to be a target of frequent or disruptive hostile state cyber activity

  • The country has some capability to detect, withstand and respond to major cyberattacks on state institutions or critical infrastructure

  • The country has a cyber intelligence agency but its capabilities to proactively detect cyber security threats are fairly limited

  • The country has a national cyber resilience strategy although it is not fully developed or implemented

  • The country has regulations on cyber breach disclosures, but this may be loosely enforced

  • The national CERT performs reasonably well by global standards on monitoring and preventing cyber and information security incidents, and assisting business sectors with security incidents and vulnerabilities

Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply.
properties.Infrastructure_Risk_risk_description:
Indicators:

  • The quality of infrastructure varies nationally

  • International and domestic airports generally have modern facilities and amenities

  • Key roads and railways are well-maintained, but other areas are neglected and may not meet demand

  • Port infrastructure is generally well-developed, of high capacity and resilient

  • The electricity supply is broadly reliable and resilientTelecommunications networks are fairly extensive and generally well-maintained

  • Fast mobile data connections may be lacking in some parts of the country, particularly remote or rural areas

  • Generally diverse and reliable supply of essential commodities, including food, medicine or fuel

  • The agencies that manage public infrastructure are generally competent and efficient, but corruption may be an issue

Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply.
properties.Domestic_Movement_Restrictions_risk_desc:
Indicators:

  • There is no nationwide directive for people to stay at home

  • There may be guidelines on self-isolation, but these are highly targeted geographically or demographically

  • Recommended closure of businesses that do not provide or produce essential goods in parts of the country

  • Public transport is operating normally for the most part

Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply.
properties.Overland_Travel_risk_description:
Indicators:

  • A moderate to high number of road accident fatalities

  • Road quality varies widely countrywide

  • Moderate volume of traffic on unpaved roads, including gravel or dirt surfaces

  • Some key roads are improperly maintained, leading to rutted surfaces and deep potholes

  • Some key roads feature difficult terrain, including winding roads and sharp corners

  • Inadequate number of road signs and traffic lights in small towns and rural areas

  • Poor nighttime visibility due to inadequate street lighting in small towns and rural areas

  • The process for obtaining a driving licence is not particularly rigorous nor transparent

  • Speed limits and other traffic laws are adequately enforced in parts of the country

  • Small makeshift vehicles or livestock are occasionally seen on key roads

  • Law enforcement officers sometimes discriminate against foreign drivers

Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply.

properties.Climatic_Risks_risk_description:
Indicators

  • There are no current warnings or alerts for high impact climatic events

  • High to severe impact climatic events are historically infrequent

  • Data indicates relatively moderate levels of material damage or numbers of people affected due to climatic events

  • There is a less than even chance that cyclonic storms will cause severe damage and danger in the coming month

  • There is a less than even chance of high-impact floods in the coming month

  • There is a less than even chance of outdoor air pollution reaching dangerous levels

  • There is a less than even chance of wildfires happening

  • There is a less than even chance of extreme temperatures

  • There is a less than even chance that droughts will dangerously affect the local population and assets in the coming month

Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply.
properties.Regime_Instability_risk_description:
Indicators:

  • Crises are frequent and the political system has underlying structural vulnerabilities, such as poor or deteriorating civil-military relations and the centralisation of power in one political body

  • Rule of law is weak, and checks and balances between the executive, legislature and judiciary are ineffective

  • The government’s control over the country and the organs of state is not fully clear and the government lacks full authority and popular legitimacy

  • Power transfers and elections are likely to see violent unrest or instability, be non-transparent and undemocratic

  • The country has a history of coups and the military and/or security agencies are prone to intervening in politics

  • The press is restricted and censored, and civil society is weak, restricted and monitored 

  • Structural weaknesses are present, such as weak institutions, high level corruption and cronyism, an autocratic political system and economic weaknesses

  • There is a high likelihood of government shutdown, administrative or legislative paralysis, electoral crises, or a cessation of public services, such as by police, the judiciary, or the civil service

Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply.
properties.Crisis_Risk_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Our information suggests that a near-term crisis is likely or highly likely; and we have some information to suggest events that might trigger a crisis are occurring or likely to occur
  • Security incidents are occurring with greater frequency than is normal and the potential for further escalation is growing
  • There is a credible risk of escalation that may occur with little warning
  • The authorities appear increasingly unable to contain destabilising events and maintain a safe and secure environment
  • Foreign governments advise against all travel and advise their nationals to consider leaving
  • There are credible warnings from official agencies of an impending or likely near term crisis event such as a geophysical (natural disaster) or medical and health related crisis
  • The sudden death or incapacitation of, or direct threat against a head of government or state has occurred in a country that has high levels of regime instability risks
  • The underlying risk of a sudden crisis is very high, even though there may be no apparent immediate risks, for example from frequent and high-impact geophysical risk events like earthquakes and tsunami
  • There are indicators of activity or intent that may indicate a sudden crisis event, such as a coup attempt or external military attack
  • Interstate conflict risks are high, and hostile powers are preparing, or signalling or betraying intent and capability to militarily attack in the near to medium term
  • Regime instability risks are high/substantial or severe and events, intelligence or analysis indicates heightened risk of coups, mutinies or insurrection
  • A state of emergency has been declared, or there are severe restrictions on movements such as curfews and lockdowns that signal or reflect a crisis threat
Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply.
properties.Covid19_Restriction_Impacts_risk_descrip:
Indicators:
  • A nationwide directive for people to stay at home or limit non-essential movement
  • Partial or countrywide ban on large gatherings
  • Mandatory closure of businesses that do not provide or produce essential goods
  • A state of emergency may be in effect in some parts of the country, but this is manifested in emergency funding rather than martial law
  • Restrictions on entry, such as mandatory 14-day self-isolation for anyone entering
  • Restrictions on exports of strategic importance
  • Schools are closed
  • Public transport is closed or severely curtailed
  • Violating restrictions on movement may result in financial penalties or arrest
properties.Civil_Unrest_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Demonstrations usually occur in a manner consistent with lawful democratic protest
  • Most protests often are of small to moderate scale, infrequent, non-violent and not widespread
  • Large but peaceful demonstrations occur sporadically
  • Demonstrations on some issues may be accompanied by localised violence
  • Rioting is uncommon
  • Public trust in government and democratic institutions is reasonably high but political movements exist with low levels of trust that incite protest
  • Socio-economic conditions are generally good but may be occasionally source of  unrest or violent dissent
  • The police are generally well-trained and disciplined, and able to contain civil disturbances but might respond to demonstrations heavy-handedly
  • Public trust in government institutions is low among certain demographic groups. 
  • The political culture probably lacks avenues for dissent to be expressed freely and the government may be unwilling to tolerate some lawful dissent 
  • There is a perception that laws are not applied and enforced fairly
  • Political participation levels are not very high and civil society may be undeveloped 
  • Trade union activity may be common and occasionally disruptive, but is generally non-militant
View the Civil Unrest risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Medical_Public_Health_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Healthcare services are of a very poor standard and cannot be relied upon, or may be critically overwhelmed.
  • There is at least one and probably more than one public health emergency that requires advanced medical and safety mitigation and other precautions.
  • The capabilities of the state to detect, prevent and respond to public health crises effectively is very low by international standards
  • Public sanitation standards are very low by international standards.
  • Very low public health expenditure per capita Trained health workers are unavailable in parts of the country
  • Only basic medical treatment is available
  • Many health professionals unable to communicate in widely spoken languages
  • Essential medicines and lifesaving resources are unavailable in parts of the country
  • Western governments advise travellers to obtain medical evacuation coverage
  • There is at least one outbreak of a communicable or other serious infectious disease
  • The WHO has declared a Grade 3 Emergency, meaning that it has substantial public health consequences and/or that substantial external support is required
  • The CDC has declared a Level 3 Travel Health Notice, meaning that it advises travellers to avoid all non-essential travel to that destination
  • Health professionals recommend specialised vaccines prior to travel
  • Global health organisations say the country has a very limited childhood immunisation program
Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply. View the Medical & Health risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Tectonic_Risks_risk_description:
Indicators
  • A relatively inactive seismic area
  • In very large countries, there are small areas relative to the size of the country that are seismically active and much higher risk
  • Earthquakes are very rarely recorded above magnitude 4
  • Seismic hazard data indicates an average geographic distribution of Peak Ground Acceleration of around 0.02-0.08 PGA (g)
  • No active volcanoes
  • Tectonic events tend to be of negligible to low impact (e.g. slight tremors causing only minor damage)
  • No exposure to tsunami risk, for example, in a landlocked country
  • Negligible to low Infrastructure Risk
Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply. See the Tectonic Risks map page for more detailed methodology information here.
properties.Governance_Risk_risk_description:
Indicators
  • Institutions are dysfunctional, the rule of law is very weak, the political system is either highly autocratic or has little legitimate authority, and may be in a state of transition or flux or crisis.
  • The state is unable to enforce law and order. Security risks are generally high and there is at least one conflict within the country. The state has lost the monopoly on organised armed violence as its authority is under direct threat
  • The government does not control many of the institutions and organs of state, or if it does exert political control over these, they lack the capacity to perform all but the most basic functions
  • Security agencies such as the military, police or intelligence, act with varying degrees of impunity and are often in competition with each other and/or the government
  • There have been frequent instances of government shutdown, administrative or legislative paralysis, electoral crises, or a cessation of public services, such as by police, the judiciary, or the civil service in the recent past
  • The press is restricted, censored and the target of violent suppression
  • Civil society (including community groups, religious organisations, unions and NGOs) is very weak and subject to threats of violence and suppression
  • The justice system is neither fair nor impartial and usually difficult for people to access; segments of the population often resort to alternative and unregulated systems of justice
  • The government struggles to formulate, legislate and enact policies to address either long or short-term challenges with little real regulation
  • The central bank has no independent authority, and/or the informal economy is so expansive that its decisions have little impact
Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply. See the Governance Risk map page for more detailed methodology information here.
properties.Cyber_Threat_Exposure_risk_description:
Indicators
  • The volume of cyber attacks on domestic networks generally occurs at levels around half of the global average, or evidence suggests that cyber attacks are relatively infrequent
  • Internet penetration is generally between 15-50% of the population
  • Smartphone penetration is generally between 10- 50% of the population
  • Social media penetration is generally between 10- 50% of the population
  • A small proportion of the population uses online banking services, or this is not a common form of banking in the country
  • The monthly average wage is in the bottom 20% of the global averages
  • Less than half of the active population possess sufficient digital skills, such as computer skills, basic coding or digital reading. Or official data on digital skills is absent.
  • There is no publicly-reported number of ransomware attacks, or the volume and impact of such attacks appear to be low in comparison with global averages
  • The country does not appear to be a target of frequent or disruptive hostile state cyber activity
Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply. See the Cyber Threat Exposure map page for more detailed methodology information here.
properties.Terrorism_Risk_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • The threat level is to low to moderate. Our analysis and information suggests that terrorists have little to some capability and/or intent to mount an attack or action
  • In the unlikely event of an attack, the capabilities of terrorists are such that attacks are likely to be small scale and of limited or no more than moderate impact
  • Moderate impact means injuries, or single casualties, limited property damage, and localised resultant disruption
  • High impact attacks mean lethal or mass casualty attacks, significant property damage, and resultant widespread disruption and loss of confidence in security beyond the location of the attack
View the Terrorism Threat and Risk maps, and explanatory notes here.
properties.Corruption_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Reported cases of petty or high level corruption are extremely common
  • Officials routinely operate with impunity
  • The rule of law has collapsed
  • Anecdotal evidence indicates malfeasance at all levels of the public sector, and solicitation of bribes and personal rewards is routine
  • The country is in a state of chaos or extreme disarray
  • Processing times for official activity, such as for operating licences and permits, is opaque and it may be impossible to acquire official permissions without violating corrupt practice laws
  • The state is effectively a criminal organisation
  • The economy is almost entirely informal
View the Corruption risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Interstate_Conflict_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • There are unresolved but non-acute territorial or sovereignty disputes with other powers  
  • Adversarial relations may exist with foreign powers that are managed through diplomatic means, although non-combat military encounters at sea, air or on land may occur in periods of heightened tension
  • Defence spending is generally consistent with economic growth and treaty obligations
  • Military capabilities are mostly defensive although it has some capability to project military force
  • The country is party to internationally recognised and functional regional cooperation agreements and/or defence alliances as part of its deterrence strategy
  • Allies may be at higher risk of armed conflict and treaty or alliance obligations may require it to deploy forces as part of a collective deterrent 
  • There is some militarisation of neighbouring countries or in the wider region that may be threatening
  • Excluding peacekeeping operations, expeditionary military capability is limited but it may maintain overseas military bases and have overseas deployments as part of a collective defence alliance
View the Interstate Conflict risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Civil_Conflict_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • There are increased activities by secessionist, separatist or other armed political movements
  • There is evidence of groups or factions arming and organising along military or paramilitary lines
  • Ethnic or religious grievances are prompting fairly frequent inter-communal violence in some parts of the country
  • Regime instability, terrorism and civil unrest risk levels are substantial or higher
  • There is a frozen civil conflict or a long-standing ceasefire between domestic factions
  • The potential for sudden armed violence within the country is high
  • There are growing levels of weapons proliferation
  • The armed forces are at risk of splitting and/or mutinies and may have a recent history of such events 
  • There is evidence of splits or factions in the armed forces or mutinies
  • Levels of militarisation and deployments are high or markedly increasing
  • Military leave is cancelled and reserves are called up
  • A state of emergency is in place
  • There is a high risk of conflict spillover or contagion from neighbouring countries
View the Civil Conflict risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Terrorism_Threat_risk_description: Our analysis and information suggests that terrorists have some capability to mount an attack in the area or on the target types indicated, and that such an act would be consistent with their general intent. View the Terrorism Threat and Risk maps, and explanatory notes here.
properties.State_Agencies_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • State agencies often target legitimate international businesses and organisations in sensitive industries for economic espionage or intelligence gathering
  • Foreigners working in potentially sensitive sectors have been arbitrarily detained in recent years and denied consular access or adequate legal representation
  • Arrests of foreigners on suspicion of espionage or subversion appear to involve fabricated and politically-motivated charges
  • Foreign governments advise against travel, and provide cautionary to stringent advice concerning electronic device security and conduct that may attract the attention of the security services
  • Foreign governments advise travellers that photographing military sites or other sensitive buildings or installations is strictly prohibited and could result in their arrest
  • The law does not protect the privacy of online activity and communications
  • The law requires private companies or individuals to assist state agencies seeking to access to the content of encrypted communications 
  • Human and other basic rights and freedoms are not respected and protected, and there is widespread suppression of social or political groups
  • The rule of law is weak. The judiciary is not impartial, inefficient and often subject to improper influence
  • Local laws are illiberal and not fully transparent and may be harshly applied
View the State Agencies risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Infrastructure_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • International and domestic airport options may be limited and tend to be a poor standard
  • Key roads are often poorly marked, unpaved, narrow or do not drain properly
  • The railway network is underdeveloped and poorly maintained, and does not meet demand
  • Roads and railways have been damaged due to armed conflict or an extreme weather event
  • Commercial shipping operating conditions are poor, and ports have limited capacity
  • Power outages are common
  • Telecommunications networks are overloaded and poorly maintained
  • Internet connectivity is slow or unavailable in parts of the countryHeavy reliance on one or two sources of fuel or other essential goods
  • There is a shortage of essential commodities, including food, medicine or fuel
  • The agencies that manage public infrastructure are mostly inefficient and corrupt
View the Infrastructure explanatory notes and risk map here.
properties.Road_Safety_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • A high number of road accident fatalities
  • High traffic volume on unpaved roads, including gravel or dirt surfaces
  • Roads with high traffic volume lack median barriers and guardrails
  • Key roads are sometimes impassable due to heavy rain or dust storms
  • Key roads feature difficult terrain, including winding roads and sharp corners
  • Inadequate number of road signs and traffic lights, even in urban areas
  • Poor nighttime visibility due to inadequate street lighting, even in urban areas
  • Aggressive or careless driving is common and rarely punished
  • The process for obtaining a driving licence is not rigorous nor transparent
  • Small makeshift vehicles or livestock are frequently seen on key roads
  • Public emergency response capabilities are underdeveloped
  • Law enforcement officers often discriminate against foreign drivers

properties.General_Crime_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Official crime data where available indicates an extremely high incidence or rates of crime
  • Foreign travel advisories indicate a very high to extreme risk of crime
  • Crime is cited anecdotally as a very serious concern by residents or visitors
  • Petty street crimes and misdemeanours are extremely common
  • Murder and other serious crime rates are an acute and widespread problem
  • Movement at night is extremely unsafe in all areas
View the General Crime risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Organised_Crime_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Organised criminal activity is widespread and law enforcement agencies are unable to counter the problem
  • Organised criminal gangs and organisations operate openly in most areas with impunity
  • Law enforcement has effectively collapsed or surrendered control to organised criminals
  • Significant and large areas are under the control of violent criminal organisations
  • Widespread proliferation of illegal firearms or other weapons.
  • Organised criminal activity is widespread and wide ranging, and commonly includes low-level and high-level crime, including fraud and financial crime, drug trafficking, street gang activity, extortion, prostitution and people trafficking, and weapons trafficking
  • The country is a major hub for organised narcotics and people trafficking
  • Evidence of widespread proliferation and trafficking of illegal firearms
  • Extremely high murder rates
  • The informal economy predominates
  • Corruption Risk levels are severe to extreme
  • Rule of law has collapsed
  • State Agencies risk is severe to critical
View the Organised Crime risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.LGBTQ_Discrimination_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Prevailing social attitudes are generally permissive and liberal
  • Consensual same-sex sexual activity is legal
  • Dissemination of pro-LGBTQ+ material is legal
  • There are laws criminalising discrimination and harassment against LGBTQ+ persons but they are not enforced consistently
  • Some interest, social or political groups experience suppression
  • LGBTQ+ persons in the country face some social stigma, particularly in more conservative areas or regions
View the LGBTQ+ Discrimination risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Kidnap_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Official crime data where available indicates that kidnap cases are very common
  • Foreign travel advisories indicate a very high threat of kidnap
  • Kidnap is cited as a serious concern by residents or visitors
  • Express kidnappings are very common and are targeted as well as opportunistic
  • There is strong evidence that organised criminal groups are engaged in kidnap for ransom, where incidents are often violent and of long duration, and sometimes fatal
  • Terrorist kidnappings are a credible threat
  • Virtual kidnap is very common
  • There are strong signs of police or other officials colluding in kidnap cases. General crime, organised crime, terrorism, state agencies and corruption levels are severe
View the Kidnap risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Security_Safety_Risk_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • All other risk levels are severe or critical, or at least one other risk or threat level is critical and renders the security or safety environment extreme risk
  • Foreign governments advise citizens not to travel and consider leaving unless they have compelling reasons to stay. In some cases, they may strongly advise or urge citizens to depart immediately by commercial means or will facilitate evacuation
  • Few if any foreign governments have diplomatic representation or provide consular services, and most embassies and consulates will be closed
  • Embassies will have tight travel restrictions for any essential expatriate staff that remain
  • Most international organisations/businesses will have activated crisis plans and withdrawn, or be in a state of withdrawing, or locking down pending safe evacuation
  • International organisations/businesses will usually have a total ban on travel unless there are exceptional circumstances that make travel essential
  • International organisations/businesses will typically take advanced mitigation measures for any activity in the country, including undertaking detailed risk assessments, stringent restrictions on movements, personal security details (from security trained drivers through to armed close protection) and requiring travellers to take hostile environment awareness training
  • International organisations/businesses will require expatriate staff that remain in-country to live in specific secure accommodation and use secure local transportation
View the Security and Safety Risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Personal_Cyber_Risk_risk_description:
Indicators
  • Host state agencies routinely target citizens and travellers to access their personal sensitive data through physical or digital means, with sensitive sectors at very high risk
  • There is a high degree of targeting opportunity and attractiveness for cyber criminals due to high levels of relative wealth
  • As an alert state, the host state may be under a period of acute stress or emergency where accessing personal devices and information of citizens or travellers is a priority
  • The country has high levels of internet, smartphone, social media and e-commerce penetration
  • The country has very high levels of social media surveillance, which could be due to bans or severe restrictions on end-to-end encryption or the country has its own social media platforms that enable it to conduct surveillance at scale
  • The country may be in a period of acute stress or a national emergency where the interception and access of personal information of citizens and foreigners may be a priority
  • The country has a ban or restrictions on end-to-end encryption messaging platforms and VPN use
  • The host state is widely known to deploy invasive spyware technology to monitor and detain specific groups, such as journalists, dissenters, LGTBQ+ persons and the political opposition
  • The country has severe restrictions or bans on the encryption of personal devices
  • The government does not allow personal use exemption of encrypted devices and it has seized devices of travellers from specific nationalities or profiles at entry/exit points or checkpoints.
  • The state agencies risk rating is severe
Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply. See the Personal Cyber Risks map page for more detailed methodology information here.

properties.Regime_Instability_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Rule of law is strong and checks and balances between the executive, legislature, and judiciary are effective and institutionally robust
  • Democratic institutions are mature and stable, and power transfers are consistently peaceful, democratic and constitutional
  • The press is free and civil society is pervasive and active 
  • If the regime is illiberal or authoritarian, it enjoys widespread and deeply entrenched popular support and legitimacy from all civil and military institutions, is long-standing (decades), and will most likely be a traditional form of government such as a monarchy
  • If the regime is illiberal or authoritarian, there are clear and robust constitutional measures for succession and a consistent history of peaceful power transfers
  • The government has full control over the country and the organs of state 
  • The military has no modern history of intervention in politics
  • The government can pass legislation, and enact policies effectively and according to due process
  • There is a remote likelihood of government shutdown, administrative or legislative paralysis, or cessation of public services, such as by police, the judiciary or the civil service

properties.Crisis_Risk_risk_description:

  • There is no evidence of a credible threat that may lead to a high impact crisis
  • Relevant local or international official agencies indicate that the risk of major crises events is low
  • Most threat and risk ratings are negligible to moderate; any that are moderate or higher, such as terrorism threat or crime, are unlikely to create acute crisis conditions
  • The government is stable and governance risks are low
  • The state is generally resilient and capable of managing reasonably foreseeable crisis events
  • There is a high degree of political and social resilience and structural stability
  • Geophysical risks are low and major geophysical risk events are uncommon or typically localised
