properties.Civil_Unrest_risk_description:
Indicators:

  • Demonstrations overwhelmingly occur in a manner consistent with lawful democratic protest 

  • Protests in nearly all cases are small to moderate scale, infrequent, non-violent and not widespread

  • Rioting is very rare

  • Public trust in government and democratic institutions is high 

  • Socio-economic conditions are good and are rarely a source of violent dissent

  • The police are well-trained and disciplined, and able to contain civil disturbances

  • The political culture is democratic and tolerant of lawful dissent 

  • Laws are applied and enforced fairly

  • Political participation levels are high and civil society is vibrant

  • Trade union activity is uncommon and non-militant

Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply.
properties.Medical_Public_Health_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Healthcare services are of a generally high standard in major cities.
  • Access to emergency healthcare services may be difficult in some locations.
  • There may be an ongoing public health emergency of limited impact. For example, an epidemic in a particular area that is being contained at present
  • The capabilities of the state to detect, prevent and respond to public health crises is average by international standards
  • Public sanitation standards are average by international standards.
  • Moderate public health expenditure per capita
  • High quality of care at private hospitals and clinics
  • Quality of care at public hospitals and clinics can be poor outside major cities
  • Specialist surgical treatment is concentrated in only one or two cities
  • Health professionals are generally able to communicate in widely spoken languages
  • Some medicines and specialised medical equipment may be unavailable in parts of the country
  • The WHO has declared a Grade 1 Emergency, meaning that it has minimal public health consequences or that minimal external support is required
  • The CDC has declared a Level 1 Travel Health Notice, meaning that it advises travellers to follow the usual precautions for that destination
  • There may be a localised outbreak of a communicable or other serious infectious disease
  • Health professionals may recommend specialised vaccines prior to travel
  • The proportion of children that receive vaccinations is high but varies countrywide
Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply. View the Medical & Health risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Tectonic_Risks_risk_description:
Indicators

  • Low probability of earthquakes occurring per annum(<10%)

  • Expected damage relatively mild (USD10mn per annum)Tsunamis unlikely to happen per annum (<5%). Expected damage below USD2mn per annum

  • Low probability of volcanic eruptions (<5% per year)

  • Low damage costs of USD0.35mn per annum

  • Low level of landslide susceptibility based on historical data

Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply.
properties.Governance_Risk_risk_description:
Indicators
  • The government, political system and state institutions are broadly stable, but may sometimes be ineffective and lack resilience and may lack high levels of public legitimacy
  • The government is reasonably effective at formulating, legislating and enacting policy, although public engagement in these processes may be limited and/or vested interests may influence policy to the detriment of wider public interest
  • Policy implementation is generally consistent although regulation may be weak or inconsistently applied
  • Legislative processes may be poor and the legislature may lack independent authority or be hamstrung, making effective legislation difficult to pass
  • Democratic institutions may not be mature or fully consolidated and in a state of transition, and vulnerable to challenges and change or erosion from populist and authoritarian governing parties, or parties that are reasonably likely to win office
  • Elections are not always wholly free and fair, and contestations of election results may be common resulting in brief periods of uncertainty and weakened public confidence in the electoral system
  • Rule of law is the general norm but is not entrenched and may be weak in some areas of governance, or it may be coming under credible attack by populist or authoritarian parties
  • The judiciary is nominally independent but can be subject to political interference. The law is generally clear and publicised, but may not be wholly stable and for some groups may not be applied evenly
  • There are low to moderate levels of state corruption, and there may be weak laws on lobbying that give interest groups a disproportionate influence on policy. Full transparency and accountability is not universal in either the elected or unelected branches of state
  • The government exercises legitimate control over the country and the organs of state, including security agencies such as the military, police and intelligence, although it may not have a full monopoly on the use of organised armed force
  • The civil service is not wholly impartial but effectively implements policy
  • Public services are of reasonable quality and reliability. There may have been rare stoppages in the provision of public services, such as by police, the judiciary or the civil service in recent history
  • Outbreaks of civil unrest and other forms of serious political violence may occur periodically, protests are generally tolerated, although some may be suppressed
  • The central bank may not be fully independent
  • The press is mostly free but the government may exert a degree of influence over some media and may use state broadcasters
  • Civil society (including community groups, religious organisations, unions and NGOs) is active but may face some constraints or monitoring on some issues, particularly press freedom and human or democratic rights
Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply. See the Governance Risk map page for more detailed methodology information here.
properties.Cyber_Threat_Exposure_risk_description:
Indicators
  • The volume of cyber attacks reported in the country generally occurs at levels that are among the lowest in the world, or evidence suggests that cyber attacks are rare
  • Internet penetration is generally less than 15% of the population
  • Smartphone penetration is generally less than 10% of the population
  • Social media penetration is generally less than 10% of the population
  • Access to online banking services is absent or very low
  • The monthly average wage is in the bottom 10% of the global averages
  • The percentage of the urban population is among the lowest in the world
  • Remote worker population is among the lowest in the world, which may be due to the economy being largely primary and secondary industries
  • There are low levels of sufficient digital skills among the active population. Or official data on digital skills is absent.
  • There is no publicly-reported number of ransomware attacks, or the volume of such attacks are negligible compared with global averages.
  • The country does not have acute tensions or is in a state of conflict with a hostile state cyber actor
Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply. See the Cyber Threat Exposure map page for more detailed methodology information here.
properties.Terrorism_Risk_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • The threat level is negligible to low. Our analysis and information suggests that terrorists have no capability and/or intent to mount an attacks anywhere in the country/city
  • Negligible to low impact means non-lethal with few if any injuries, little if any property damage, no wider disruption, and no effect on the wider security environment
  • High impact attacks mean lethal or mass casualty attacks, significant property damage, and resultant widespread disruption and loss of confidence in security beyond the location of the attack
View the Terrorism Threat and Risk maps, and explanatory notes here.
properties.Corruption_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Reported cases of petty or high level corruption are uncommon
  • The rule of law is generally established but may be inconsistent in some areas
  • Public service provision is of a reasonable quality
  • Regulations can sometimes be excessive
  • Officials are not always held accountable for misconduct
  • Anecdotal evidence indicates state representatives sometimes expect abnormal cash ‘facilitation payments’
  • Administrative procedures are non-transparent
  • Processing times for official activity, such as for operating licences and permits, are sometimes clear and not always adhered to
  • There is a large informal economy
View the Corruption risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Interstate_Conflict_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Peaceful international relations
  • No territorial or sovereignty disputes or adversarial relations with other states
  • Neighbouring or regional powers have no military buildups or offensive capabilities in border areas
  • Large-scale military exercises are infrequent and conducted internationally in a peacetime defence framework as joint exercises with neighbours and allies
  • The government has international legitimacy and recognition
  • The country is party to internationally recognised and functional regional co-operation agreements and/or defence alliances
  • Militarisation of neighbouring countries and in the wider region is low
  • Low levels of defence spending 
  • Military capabilities are entirely defensive
  • Excluding peacekeeping operations, little to no expeditionary military capability or overseas military bases
View the Interstate Conflict risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Civil_Conflict_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • There are no armed groups active in the country
  • Inter-communal violence is very rare
  • Regime instability, terrorism, and civil unrest risk levels are very low
  • The government has legitimacy and authority
  • The military is professional, stable, cohesive and disciplined
  • Regime instability and civil unrest risk ratings are negligible to low
  • There is no risk of conflict spillover or contagion from neighbouring countries
View the Civil Conflict risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Terrorism_Threat_risk_description: Our analysis and information suggests that terrorists have no capability and/or intent to mount an attack/s in the area or on the target types indicated in the assessment. View the Terrorism Threat and Risk maps, and explanatory notes here.
properties.State_Agencies_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • State agencies have little to no known intent to target legitimate international companies and organisations or their personnel for economic espionage or intelligence gathering
  • The government is not noted as being hostile to or suspicious of visitors, expatriates or businesses from particular countries
  • The host state is not known to have delayed or otherwise interfered with consular access to a detained foreigner or with their legal representation in recent years
  • Any arrests of foreigners on suspicion of espionage or subversion do not appear to involve fabricated or politically-motivated charges
  • Foreign governments provide generic or no advice concerning electronic device security, or advice and safety guidelines regarding conduct that may attract the attention of the security services
  • The law protects the privacy of online activity and communications
  • The rule of law is strong. The judiciary is impartial and efficient and free of improper influence
  • State agencies operate with checks and balances, and intelligence and security services are subject to independent oversight
  • Local laws are generally liberal and transparent, and human and other basic rights and freedoms are generally respected and protected by the state
  • The corruption risk rating is negligible or low
View the State Agencies risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Infrastructure_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • The quality of infrastructure varies nationally
  • International and domestic airports generally have modern facilities and amenities
  • Key roads and railways are well-maintained, but other areas are neglected and may not meet demand
  • Port infrastructure is generally well-developed, of high capacity and resilient
  • The electricity supply is broadly reliable and resilientTelecommunications networks are fairly extensive and generally well-maintained
  • Fast mobile data connections may be lacking in some parts of the country, particularly remote or rural areas
  • Generally diverse and reliable supply of essential commodities, including food, medicine or fuel
  • The agencies that manage public infrastructure are generally competent and efficient, but corruption may be an issue
View the Infrastructure explanatory notes and risk map here.
properties.Road_Safety_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • A moderate to high number of road accident fatalities
  • Road quality varies widely countrywide
  • Moderate volume of traffic on unpaved roads, including gravel or dirt surfaces
  • Some key roads are improperly maintained, leading to rutted surfaces and deep potholes
  • Some key roads feature difficult terrain, including winding roads and sharp corners
  • Inadequate number of road signs and traffic lights in small towns and rural areas
  • Poor nighttime visibility due to inadequate street lighting in small towns and rural areas
  • The process for obtaining a driving licence is not particularly rigorous nor transparent
  • Speed limits and other traffic laws are adequately enforced in parts of the country
  • Small makeshift vehicles or livestock are occasionally seen on key roads
  • Law enforcement officers sometimes discriminate against foreign drivers
View the Road Safety methodology and explanatory notes here.
properties.General_Crime_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Official crime data where available indicates a moderate incidence or rates of crime
  • Foreign travel advisories indicate a generally low to moderate risk of crime
  • Crime is generally not cited anecdotally as a serious concern by residents or visitors
  • Petty street crimes and misdemeanors are the main threats and may be common in some areas
  • Murder and other serious crime rates are a problem in some areas
  • Movement at night is generally safe, but may be unsafe in some areas
View the General Crime risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Organised_Crime_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • There are some identified organised criminal groups or networks
  • Organised criminal activity is generally limited by effective law enforcement agencies, and tends not to significantly affect legitimate international businesses, but local business may encounter issues
  • Organised criminal activity includes low-level and some high-level crime, including fraud and financial crime, drug trafficking, street gang activity in urban areas, extortion, prostitution and people trafficking, low levels of weapons trafficking and other crimes within the sphere of general crime
  • Violent control of territory may be an issue in some urban areas
  • Some evidence of organised proliferation of illegal firearms
  • Corruption Risk levels are low to moderate
  • Rule of law is relatively strong
  • State Agencies risk is moderate
View the Organised Crime risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.LGBTQ_Discrimination_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Prevailing social attitudes are predominantly permissive and liberal
  • Consensual same-sex sexual activity is legal
  • Dissemination of pro-LGBTQ+ material is legal
  • There are laws criminalising discrimination and harassment against LGBTQ+ persons and they are usually enforced consistently
  • Full legal recognition of same-sex marriage
  • Legal recognition of gender identity or non-binary gender
  • The rule of law is very strong
View the LGBTQ+ Discrimination risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Kidnap_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Official crime data where available indicates that kidnaps are uncommon but do occur
  • Foreign travel advisories indicate a risk of some types of kidnap, usually limited to certain areas
  • Kidnap is only occasionally cited as a concern by residents or visitors in some areas
  • Most incidents that occur are isolated cases and are non-professional, such a family, acquaintance or child abductions
  • Financially-motivated kidnappings are in nearly all cases opportunistic and of limited duration such as express kidnap
  • General crime, organised crime, state agencies and corruption levels are moderate
View the Kidnap risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Security_Safety_Risk_risk_description:
Indicators:
  • Most other risk ratings are negligible to moderate, but some may be higher such as terrorism or general crime
  • Foreign governments have no travel restrictions but advise caution in some or all areas for citizens
  • Foreign governments have diplomatic representation, full staffing usually with dependents, and have no travel restrictions in place for their expatriate staff
  • International organisations/businesses have few, if any, travel restrictions but may require their travellers to follow country-specific safety advice or stay in accommodation that conforms to increased levels of security and safety requirements
  • International organisations/businesses will not usually require expatriate staff to live in approved accommodation or locations or travel locally with security, but may issue security guidance
View the Security and Safety Risk map and explanatory notes here.
properties.Personal_Cyber_Risk_risk_description:
Indicators
  • Host state agencies are not noted for targeting the domestic population or travellers to access personal sensitive data through physical or digital means, such as spyware
  • There is a lack of targeting opportunity and attractiveness for cyber criminal groups due to low levels of internet usage and the average wealth of the population
  • Internet penetration is generally less than 15% of the population
  • State agencies have little to no known intent to conduct hostile surveillance or intercept data of its citizens and travellers for intelligence purposes
  • The host state has very low levels of social media surveillance, and is not known to pressure social media platforms to provide user information or take down content
  • The host state is not known to possess state-developed or commercial spyware technology
  • Smartphone penetration is generally less than 10% of the population
  • There are very low levels of government filtering of the internet
  • The host state is not known to conduct arrests of online users, or the level of such activity is very low
  • The host state has little to no restrictions on the encryption of personal devices
  • The government supports the personal use exemption of encrypted devices
  • The state agencies risk rating is negligible to low
  • The organised crime risk rating is negligible to low
Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply. See the Personal Cyber Risks map page for more detailed methodology information here.
properties.National_Cyber_Resilience_risk_descripti:
Indicators

  • The government provides no support to business sectors

  • The country is among the lowest ranked in its preparedness to prevent cyber threats and respond to cyber incidents, based on official and intergovernmental datasets

  • The country has demonstrated no capability to detect, withstand and respond to major cyberattacks on state institutions or critical infrastructure

  • The country does not have a cyber intelligence agency and is unable to detect cyber security threats

  • The country does not have a national cyber resilience strategy and there is no indication it is moving towards developing one

  • The country has no framework for cyber breach disclosures

  • The country has no national CERT, and no capabilities to assist business sectors with cybersecurity incidents and vulnerabilities

Risk levels are determined by the risk level definition and body of indicators that best describe the level of risk relative to other risk levels. Not all indicators necessarily apply.
